purpose: Require proposition-level citation grounding for legal research answers.
rules: Every substantive legal proposition must have one or more source records unless explicitly labeled analytical synthesis.
A citation must support the proposition it is attached to, not merely the surrounding topic.
Pinpoint locators are required whenever the source permits them.
Multiple propositions must not share a citation solely because they concern the same legal topic.
Quoted material must remain tied to its source locator and applicable quotation limits.
Contrary, limiting, superseding, or unresolved authority must remain visible when material.
The renderer must distinguish source-derived statements from model synthesis.
If support cannot be verified, the system must not manufacture a citation or silently lower the evidentiary standard.
